sentences.text: Members of the Capnocytophaga genus are described as common residents of the oral cavity of humans and of some animals, notably dogs and cats.
A metapangenomic study of the human oral cavity reported a strong preference of most Capnocytophaga genomes for dental plaque, both supragingival and subgingival.
That study identified strain-level variants of C. sputigena, C. gingivalis, C. granulosa and C. leadbetteri that were detected more often on the tongue.
A narrative review notes increasing reports linking certain human oral-associated Capnocytophaga species with systemic infections, while stating that clinical data are currently scanty.
